learning: If s-bend progress rises above 0.26 and oscillation stays near 0.28 to 0.3, mass is a real lever toward the lighter side. If oscillation rises sharply (toward iteration 4's 0.33) with no progress gain, the mass floor is near 0.6 kg and remaining gains must come from the controller.
notes: Single-variable mass test on the iteration-1 controller, so the result compares directly with iteration 1 (114.4). Controller unchanged on purpose to keep the test clean.
rationale: The Builder's geometry tests mass 0.5 kg on the iteration-1 design. Iteration 9 (0.8 kg) cut s-bend progress from 0.26 to 0.16 and the score from 114.4 to 106.0, so heavier yaw inertia slows the bends. Iteration 4 cut mass to 0.5 kg but also changed radius, length and speed, and oscillation rose to 0.33. The lighter-mass direction has not been isolated. I therefore keep the controller exactly at iteration-1 values (base_speed 1.5, kp 2.5, ki 0, kd 0.30, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], last_direction). Any score change then comes from mass alone. Lower mass may raise steering oscillation, but I will not add damping in the same race, because that would confound the test. The geometry matches the Builder's proposal exactly: 5 sensors at x = -0.05 to +0.05 (0.025 m spacing), y = 0.03 m, 12 mm footprint, wheel_track 0.10 m, wheel_radius 0.035 m, body 0.14 x 0.10 m, mass 0.5 kg. Expected result, not measured: s-bend progress at or above 0.26, oval progress near 0.47, and oscillation near or below about 0.3. Risk: a lighter robot may overshoot more on bends.
